text: Write a program that shows the difference between copying a value and copying a reference. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___;  b = 99;                       // copy the value, then change the copy
explanation: Verified: a = 1, p[0] = 99. Same syntax, opposite outcome. `b = a` copies a number; `q = p` copies an arrow, and both arrows then point at one array. This is the single most consequential asymmetry in the language for a beginner, and Chapter 20 gives it a name — aliasing — and an argument about when it is what you wanted.
